ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners against the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) domestic terrorist list, United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the UK Sanctions List. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any Politically Exposed Person (PEP) or anyone with a familial or close-corporate relationship to a PEP, in accordance with section 35 and section 38 of the Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Prevention Act 2007. A reasonable adverse-media and source-of-funds analysis must be documented and retained. The screening must be repeated at least every 90 days while the company is in formation process.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) official company registry portal – www.sifa.gov.ws (electronic filing interface operated by the Registrar of International Companies, Apia; agent-assisted filing requirement for all International Companies)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All statutory company names must be recorded in the Roman/Latin script, with standard English language corporate suffixes. The name must be readable and pronounceable under the English alphabet; Chinese characters, Sino-alphabetic pinyin strings without semantic English reflection, and non-Roman scripts are prohibited in the registered legal name. A Chinese character-only translation may be used as an unregistered trading name, but such trading style must not be the sole expression of the legal name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a requested company name, the licensed Samoan registered agent may file a written administrative appeal with the Registrar of International Companies at SIFA within 14 days of the rejection notice. The appeal must set out the proposed name, the statutory basis for belief that the name is not prohibited, and a legal argument distinguishing any conflicting registry entry. If the Registrar fails to grant a favorable determination, the applicant may file a secondary appeal to the Finance Minister of Samoa within 30 days of the refusal, invoking section 8(3) of the International Companies Act 1987. A full re-filing with a substantially different name is permitted without penalty, but a new reservation fee is charged and the 30-day reservation clock resets.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted for International Companies under the Samoa International Finance Authority Act and International Companies Act 1987. A physical registered office in Samoa, maintained by a licensed registered agent or Samoan law firm, is required at the address on the certificate of incorporation. All statutory registers, minute books, and UBO records must be available for inspection at that physical address. Online or virtual-only service addresses are not accepted by SIFA.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-again-unannounced risk. SIFA compliance officers and the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit retain statutory authority to conduct unannounced inspections of the registered office, corporate books, and physical records. For a low-risk foreign-owned CAD/BIM outsourcing vehicle with no local license and no public solicitation, the estimated probability of an on-site physical inspection during the first financial year is 10-15%, but increases to 30-35% if any payment-rail exception, PEP, or adverse-media signal appears during due diligence.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2008, specifically sections 4 (application for incorporation), 6 (issuance of certificate of incorporation), 7 (memorandum and articles), 9 (registered office), 10 (registered agent), 32 (directors) and related provisions dealing with the register of members. International Companies are expressly exempt from applicable Samoa stamp duty and income tax under the International Companies Act 1987.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form IC-1 Application for Incorporation of an International Company together with the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for a Samoa International Company. Share capital may be denominated in any currency, commonly USD, and there is no requirement to deposit capital into an escrow or blocked account. The licensed registered agent must, however, verify the lawful source of subscription funds as part of its Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2007 obligations.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) the share capital subscribed in the Memorandum of Association be and is hereby allotted to the subscribers as set out in the Register of Members; (2) the registered office in Apia, Samoa maintained by the licensed registered agent be and is hereby adopted as the Company's statutory registered office; (3) the persons named in the Statement of Directors and Officers be and are hereby appointed first director and first secretary; and (4) the directors and the registered agent be authorized to file the company returns with the Samoa International Finance Authority, open bank accounts, and execute ancillary documents for the offshore CAD/BIM engineering consultancy business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engagement of SIFA-Licensed Registered Agent and Pre-Incorporation AML/KYC Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA-licensed International Company service provider (registered agent), Apia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute an engagement letter with a licensed registered agent, who performs KYC/AML due diligence on all directors, shareholders and beneficial owners, confirms the proposed corporate name, collects fees and dossiers, and acts as the statutory intermediary for all SIFA filings.
required_dossiers: Certified passport copy of each director, shareholder and beneficial owner
Notarized proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement dated less than 3 months)
Bank reference letter or independent professional reference
Curriculum vitae or corporate profile of each director and shareholder
Signed engagement letter with the licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The registered agent will request supplementary KYC evidence and hold the file for 14 days; if evidence remains incomplete, the engagement terminates and any fees paid are refunded less disbursements.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Filing of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Apia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent submits Form IC-1, the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association, and consent forms through the SIFA Registry. The Registrar checks name availability and acceptability; any restricted word requires regulatory approval before incorporation.
required_dossiers: Form IC-1 Application for Incorporation of an International Company
Memorandum and Articles of Association (English)
Consent to act as director
Consent to act as secretary
Consent of the registered agent to act as registered office holder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the name or articles, the agent amends and refiles the documents within 30 days. If incorporation is refused, an appeal lies to the Supreme Court of Samoa with leave under the International Companies Act 1987.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Incorporation Fee and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA Registry, Apia (with fee collection by the Samoa Ministry of Finance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon clearance of the application, the registered agent pays the prescribed USD 200 government incorporation fee on behalf of the client. The Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation bearing the company registration number and date of incorporation, and enters the company on the International Companies Register.
required_dossiers: SIFA fee receipt
Approved Memorandum and Articles of Association
Certificate of Incorporation (issued by SIFA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Administrative errors on the certificate are corrected by written request to the Registrar; a refusal to rectify is appealable to the Supreme Court of Samoa.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of First Board Resolution, Appointment of Officers and Establishment of Statutory Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors, acting at the registered office in Apia or by written resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The directors pass the pro-forma First Board Resolution allotting the initial shares, adopting the registered office and appointing the first director and secretary. The statutory registers of members, directors, officers and charges, together with share certificates, are prepared and maintained at the registered office. The beneficial ownership register is compiled and made available to SIFA through the registered agent under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2007.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma First Board Resolution (original)
Register of members reflecting the initial allotment
Register of directors and officers
Beneficial ownership register and declaration
Share certificates (scrip)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any deficient resolution is ratified by a subsequent written resolution of the directors; incorrect register entries are corrected retroactively by board minute and, where required, by re-filing with SIFA via the registered agent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Certificates and Tax-Exempt Confirmation for Banking and Client Onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent requests a Certificate of Good Standing, a Certificate of Incumbency and a statement confirming the International Company's zero-tax status under the International Companies Act 1987. These instruments support the corporate bank account opening package (wire transfer and Wise onboarding) and the customer due diligence review by offshore engineering clients.
required_dossiers: Request letter from the licensed registered agent
Certificate of Incorporation (certified copy)
Certificate of Good Standing (issued by SIFA)
Certificate of Incumbency (issued by SIFA)
Tax exemption or tax status confirmation letter (issued by SIFA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SIFA withholds certification due to outstanding annual compliance, the agent settles the outstanding annual license fee of USD 200 and any penalty, and obtains the certificates upon reinstatement of the company's good standing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable. Offshore engineering CAD/BIM service delivery is exempt from the onshore Business Licences Act 1998 regime administered by the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL). The sole statutory regulator of a Samoa International Company is the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA). No manufacturing, industrial or construction permit applies to ISIC 7110 activity performed exclusively offshore.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required. No business licence or industrial operating permit is imposed on International Companies for offshore architectural and engineering CAD/BIM activities. The company may, for client-facing convenience, obtain an SIFA-issued Certificate of Good Standing evidencing compliance.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA), Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt. The proposed activity is a purely administrative office function with no physical project footprint, land disturbance or construction works in Samoa; therefore no EIA Registration and no Full EIA Report is triggered under the Planning and Urban Management Act 2004.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC emissions, hazardous waste or regulated pollutants are generated by the offshore drafting activity. Any general office waste must be handled in accordance with the Waste Management Act 2007; incidental sanitary wastewater from the registered office must meet Samoa Water Authority sewer standards under the Water Resources Management Act 2008. SIFA imposes no environmental conditions on International Companies.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA) for the registered-office premises; building occupancy and structural load clearance from the Ministry of Works, Transport and Infrastructure (MWTI); and occupational health and safety compliance under the Labour and Employment Relations Act 2013 for any physical staff. For a purely offshore International Company, reliance on the registered agent's certified office premises satisfies these requirements.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue, Government of Samoa (MfR), Apia, Samoa; online portal: www.revenue.gov.ws (Samoa Tax Administration System - STAS, enabling TIN issuance, VAGST registration, and e-filing of VAT returns). Incorporation and International Company (IC) licensing are administered separately by the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), a division of the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), via the Samoa Companies Office.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Samoa International Company (IC) incorporated under the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended) is statutorily exempt from all Samoa taxes (income tax, VAGST, stamp duty, capital gains tax, and withholding taxes) on its international business, and therefore has no mandatory obligation to obtain a TIN from MfR. However, to recover VAGST on incidental local purchases (e.g., office rent, utilities, professional fees), the IC may voluntarily register: Step 1 - incorporate the IC through a SIFA-licensed registered agent: name clearance, lodgement of Memorandum and Articles of Association, Certificate of Incorporation, and payment of prescribed incorporation fee (approx. WST 500-1,500); Step 2 - receive the IC Registration Number from SIFA and the Certificate of Exemption; Step 3 - if desired, submit Form VAT-01 (Application for Registration) plus the Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum & Articles, power of attorney from non-resident director, and registered agent confirmation letter to MfR, who will issue a TIN and eligible VAGST certificate; Step 4 - maintain no income tax registration; the IC remains outside the MfR income tax return net. For a domestic Samoa company (fallback structure), the SOP would be: company incorporation under Companies Act 2006, then TIN application via STAS, corporate income tax registration, PAYE registration, VAGST registration if annual taxable turnover exceeds WST 100,000, and a business license from the Samoa Tourism Authority or Ministry of Revenue where applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone (International Company). The IC is exempt from all income tax and duties under the International Companies Act 1987, section 180 (as amended): zero percent income tax on all offshore-derived income, including fees from civil infrastructure BIM/CAD services supplied to non-resident clients; exemption from VAGST on offshore supplies; exemption from stamp duty on all instruments and transactions; no withholding tax on dividends, interest, royalties, or management fees paid to non-residents; no capital gains tax; no annual income tax return filing obligation; exemption valid indefinitely while the IC remains compliant with SIFA annual renewal fees and does not breach the domestic trading prohibition (i.e., no business with Samoa residents, no ownership of local real property except a 30-year lease of office premises, no import/export of physical goods within Samoa).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists under Samoa law; entity classification follows statute, not election. A Samoa IC is automatically tax-exempt; no affirmative election is required. Optional elections available: (1) Domestic company re-domiciliation - an IC may elect under Part XIV of the International Companies Act to convert into a domestic company under the Companies Act 2006, voluntarily subjecting itself to 25% corporate income tax and VAGST in exchange for access to Samoa's Double Tax Agreements (currently limited to a network of fewer than 10 DTA partners, e.g., Australia, New Zealand, Norway, Thailand, UAE); (2) Voluntary VAGST registration - an IC providing offshore services may elect to register for VAGST at a turnover below the statutory threshold to claim input tax credits on local purchases; the election is subject to MfR approval and cannot be withdrawn for 24 months; (3) No hybrid mismatch, CFC, or controlled foreign company election is available; Samoa has not enacted OECD hybrid mismatch rules; (4) No group consolidation election exists; each IC is taxed independently and is separately exempt.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST) under the Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act 2003 (as amended) and administered under the Tax Administration Act 2012; nominal reference rate set by the Minister for Revenue.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 in taxable supplies in any 12-month rolling period (mandatory registration threshold). Voluntary registration is available to any person making or intending to make taxable supplies, including an IC, with MfR consent. A Samoa International Company supplying offshore BIM/CAD services to non-residents is not subject to VAGST on that offshore supply because the place of supply rule in the VAGST Act 2003, section 9, treats services supplied to a non-resident who is outside Samoa and whose benefit is received wholly outside Samoa as outside the scope of Samoa VAGST; accordingly, the IC has no mandatory VAGST registration requirement, and any such registration is only elective for input recovery purposes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, government-operated e-invoicing API, or digital stamping regime is operational in Samoa as of the 2025 filing season. MfR operates an indirect, post-transaction control model: registered persons must file electronic VAT returns (Form VAT-200) through STAS and retain supporting tax invoices. Tax invoice requirements (VAGST Act 2003, section 24 and VAGST Regulations 2004): sequential numbering, supplier name and TIN, recipient name and TIN (if registered), date of supply, clear description, quantity and unit price, VAGST amount shown separately, total amount, and the words 'Tax Invoice'. E-invoicing in standard PDF/XML format is accepted; no digital signature, barcode, or real-time transmission is mandated. MfR is, however, developing an electronic fiscal device framework for tourism and retail sectors only, which does not affect offshore service exporters or ICs.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under VAGST Act 2003, section 16(1)(a)-(h), zero-rating (0% VAGST) applies to: (a) exports of goods (provided the exporter retains proof of physical export and legal ownership passes to the non-resident); (b) services supplied to a non-resident who is outside Samoa at the time services are performed and where the benefit is enjoyed entirely outside Samoa; (c) services directly related to land or goods situated outside Samoa; (d) internationally transported goods and passengers; (e) goods sold to approved non-resident diplomatic missions; and (f) supplies to prescribed international development organizations. For the civil infrastructure BIM/CAD and structural drafting service scope of ISIC 7110: the IC must evidence that the client is a non-resident developer, civil contractor, or engineering consultancy; the drafting software and servers may be located in Samoa but the intellectual output is delivered electronically to the offshore client; the contract must state that the place of supply is the client's jurisdiction; the service must not be connected to any site, building, or infrastructure asset located in Samoa; and the IC must maintain full technical evidence of delivery (server logs, email transmission records, cloud delivery confirmations). An IC does not need to claim zero-rating because its offshore income is wholly outside the scope of VAGST and tax-exempt at the entity level; the zero-rating provisions above apply principally to registered domestic Samoa exporters of similar engineering services, allowing them to recover input VAGST while charging 0% output tax.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Samoa Customs Export Declaration (electronic SAD-equivalent via ASYCUDA World) - only applicable for physical goods; for pure offshore services, a 'No Customs Entry Required' letter from the Samoa Customs Service
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export from Samoa (for any hybrid physical deliverables such as printed drawing sets or model files shipped on media)

Inward Remittance Certificate / Foreign Currency Credit Advice from a licensed Samoa commercial bank confirming receipt of payment from the non-resident client via Wire Transfer or Wise in USD, AUD, NZD, or EUR
Signed Service Agreement / Work Order between the IC and the non-resident client describing the BIM/CAD scope, milestone delivery schedule, and place-of-supply clause
Electronic Delivery Logs: email transmittal, cloud repository (BIM 360/Autodesk Construction Cloud) access records, and file-hosting confirmation
Residency Status Evidence of the client: certificate of incorporation, tax residency certificate, or utility bill demonstrating non-resident status
VAGST Tax Invoice issued by the IC (if registered) showing 0% rate and zero-rating statutory reference
SIFA Certificate of Exemption for the IC confirming the exempt-zone classification
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: MfR audit powers under Tax Administration Act 2012 allow a 5-year review window from the VAT return due date, extendable to 10 years in cases of assumed fraud. Penalty framework: (1) late payment penalty of 1.5% per month on any VAGST shortfall; (2) shortfall penalty of 25% of the assessed tax for failure to take reasonable care, 75% for intentional disregard of the law, and 150% for fraudulent conduct; (3) statutory interest at the annual prescribed rate (currently 12%) compounded monthly; (4) clawback of any VAGST input credits claimed without proper zero-rated export substantiation, with retrospective effect to the date of the incorrect claim; (5) criminal sanction: a person who knowingly claims fraudulent export zero-rating is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding WST 100,000 or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 5 years, or both; (6) for an International Company specifically, the more serious clawback is the loss of exempt-zone status: if the IC is found to have derived any Samoa domestic source income, or to have traded with a Samoa resident, SIFA may deregister the IC and MfR will retrospectively impose 25% corporate income tax on all assessable income plus penalties and interest, with no statute of limitation for tax evasion. MfR and SIFA share a joint risk-based audit protocol targeting shell ICs that transact with Asia-Pacific engineering contractors; documentary insufficiency is presumptive evidence of a domestic supply reversing the export zero-rating or the tax exemption.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS; Samoan: Faletupe Tutotonu o Samoa) — the sole monetary authority and prudential regulator of Samoa, established under the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984; it administers the Exchange Control Act 1972 and the Exchange Control Regulations 1977, operating through CBS-licensed Authorized Foreign Exchange Dealers, being exclusively the licensed commercial banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Samoa maintains a managed-float Samoan Tala (WST) with limited formal convertibility governed by an exchange-control licensing regime. Current-account inflows, comprising revenues from exported CAD/BIM engineering services, are freely receivable through authorized dealers with documentary support; current-account outflows, including sub-contract design fees, software licensing and professional charges, are permitted against standard invoice evidence. Capital-account transactions require prior CBS approval or post-facto notification lodged through the onboarding bank. A Samoa International Company (IC) is treated as a non-resident entity for exchange-control purposes and may lawfully retain USD/EUR/NZD/AUD receipts in foreign-currency accounts at an authorized dealer; profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is processed only after verification of audited financial statements, a books-and-records declaration demonstrating substantive accounting, and settlement of any Samoan tax or statutory liability. The WST has no robust offshore deliverable market, so hedging and repatriation discipline rely on onshore forwards and multi-currency account management rather than deep NDF liquidity.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Statutory timeline and conversion ratio: (i) resident-export businesses under the Exchange Control Act 1972 must repatriate all export receipts to a CBS-licensed bank within 90 days from the payment-due date or invoice date, whichever is earlier; (ii) the mandatory conversion ratio for resident exporters is 100% surrender to the authorized dealer in WST unless the CBS grants a Foreign Currency Retention Facility, under which approved exporters may retain up to 100% of USD proceeds for up to 12 months; (iii) the WS_IC, being a non-resident offshore International Company prohibited from trading with Samoan residents, is outside the strict mandatory-surrender discipline: it may retain the entirety of its CAD/BIM service receipts in a USD Foreign Currency Account at a licensed dealer, but must nonetheless clear all incoming SWIFT settlements through a Samoa-licensed bank for balance-of-payments statistical reporting and complete a 90-day internal repatriation reconciliation with the relationship manager; (iv) any USD-to-WST conversion executed to fund local statutory expenses must be transacted at the authorized dealer's prevailing market rate and declared on the CBS exchange-control return on a T+1 basis.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Legacy corporate accounts only; no new Capital Escrow or Operational Account openings available

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: MEDIUM-LOW, restricted auxiliary rail only. No offshore EMI is licensed as an Authorized Foreign Exchange Dealer in Samoa; therefore Wise or other offshore digital EMI accounts cannot legally serve as the primary treasury repository or perform CBS-recognized FX conversion, and balances parked in an offshore EMI for more than 90 days create a technical exchange-control breach against the Samoa export-proceeds repatriation expectation. Viable use: a secondary collections rail for small-ticket CAD/BIM milestone invoices from dispersed international clients, with funds received in USD at Wise and swept by MT103 to the BSP USD Foreign Currency Account on a maximum T+3 net-liquidity cycle, each sweep matched to an invoice and reported to the bank as incoming service receipts. Legal constraints: EMI onboarding requires the WS_IC UBO passports, board authorization, and an executed terms-of-service acknowledging that Samoa exchange-control obligations apply; the EMI cannot hold WST; and the EMI must never be used for equity injections, dividend repatriation, or intercompany capital movements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person appearance remains the prevailing standard. Under the Samoa AML/CFT regime, administered by the CBS and the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit, the beneficial owner and at least one corporate director or authorized signatory must appear physically at the Apia branch for biometric verification, or before a designated BSP group branch in an acceptable jurisdiction with formal video-link attestation by the bank's MLRO. Pure remote opening is not accepted for unlisted International Companies. Required persons and instruments: (i) each natural-person UBO; (ii) certified and apostillized Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Good Standing (less than 3 months old), and Memorandum/Articles, with a Chinese-language certified translation where the constitutional documents are issued bilingually; (iii) registry extract demonstrating the IC's filing compliance with the Registrar of International Companies under the Samoa International Finance Authority framework; (iv) board resolution opening the account and defining the signatory matrix; (v) Certificate of Incumbency issued by the licensed corporate or trust service provider; and (vi) 3 to 6 months of banking references. Where the UBO cannot travel, the CBS-accepted alternative is identification certification before a Samoa consular officer or a BSP correspondent in Hong Kong, followed by an in-person video interview and courier-consolidated original documents; final AML/CFT sign-off remains with the local bank MLRO and is granted only where a demonstrable economic-substance file is maintained.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The Samoa IC is classified as an offshore tax-exempt shell; beneficial ownership is held through a Chinese family trust, triggering the classic shell-company red flag at the relationship-management filter.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Substance Pack: (i) Certificate of Incorporation and current Certificate of Good Standing issued by the Samoa Registrar of International Companies; (ii) full UBO and ownership-chain schematic naming every natural person, trust, protector and trustee with percentage shareholding, matched to apostillized passports; (iii) board resolution and signatory schedule; (iv) Certificate of Incumbency and trust-deed summary issued by the SIFA-licensed corporate-services or trustee company; (v) filed annual-return records confirming the IC is in good regulatory standing; (vi) executed engineering-services master agreements, sample CAD/BIM deliverables, and client-side confirmations evidencing real commercial operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds uncertainty for the initial equity subscription; funds arriving from the family trust through a Hong Kong treasury vehicle appear without prior transaction history at the Samoan dealership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-Funds and Source-of-Wealth Pack: (i) 12-month bank statements of the subscribing entity or trust showing accumulation trace; (ii) trust deed, trust accounts, and trustee resolution approving the subscription; (iii) executed share-subscription agreement and share-allotment resolution; (iv) original SWIFT MT103 advice evidencing the complete wire path from the Hong Kong treasury into BSP; (v) personal and corporate tax-clearance certificates of the UBOs from their home jurisdictions; (vi) notarized declaration of wealth and source of the trust corpus signed by settlor and protector.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Correspondent-banking flag on repetitive low-value outgoing wires to mainland-China BIM sub-contractors creates sanctions-screening and trade-based money-laundering narrative.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Trade Services Pack: (i) dual-language master outsourcing agreement between the WS_IC and the PRC delivery entity with per-deliverable pricing; (ii) three completed transaction samples matched as invoice, inbound MT103 receipt, and sub-contractor remittance advice; (iii) CAD/BIM file-delivery logs and time-stamped model exports; (iv) the IC's internal know-your-counterparty AML declaration for each PRC beneficiary; (v) CBS export-of-services reporting slips filed by the bank for the corresponding inbound settlements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The account doubles as a family-office treasury for multi-jurisdictional asset preservation, raising account-monitoring and anti-commingling concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury Governance Pack: (i) board-approved treasury and anti-commingling policy restricting all outflows to invoiced operational costs or statutory items; (ii) six-month transaction ledger pre-cleared by an external CPA demonstrating one-to-one invoice mapping; (iii) lease, payroll, and software-subscription contracts evidencing business nexus and costs; (iv) monthly reconciliation signed by the independent auditor; (v) written undertaking to the bank's AML/CFT officer to provide semi-annual management accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exemption abuse suspicion: the banker must distinguish the IC's legitimate zero-tax offshore status from unlawful evasion routed through the domestic banking system.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tax Compliance Pack: (i) written legal opinion confirming the IC's non-resident classification and tax-exempt treatment under the International Companies Act 1987 and the applicable Income Tax Ordinance exemption map; (ii) retained proper accounting records maintained in Apia satisfying the statutory books-and-records test; (iii) tax-clearance certificates for any Samoa payroll or GST nexus; (iv) signed declaration that no Samoa-resident person is served and no Samoan real property is held; (v) commitment to circulate six-monthly management accounts to the relationship manager.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Primary rail: SWIFT MT103 (or MT202/COV for same-day high-value clearing through a US or ANZ/NZD clearer) from the subscribing family trust or Hong Kong treasury account to BSP's correspondent, then booked to the WS_IC USD Capital Escrow sub-account. Field-level protocol: Field 50K remitter must exactly match the UBO or trust name recorded in the KYC file; Field 59 beneficiary must match the account mandate; Field 70 purpose text must read 'REM//INWARD DIRECT INVESTMENT EQUITY SUBSCRIPTION, INTERNATIONAL COMPANIES ACT 1987'; the receiving dealer maps the remittance to the Samoa balance-of-payments classification 'Direct Investment — Equity Capital' and to the CBS exchange-control inward-investment record. Verification protocol: the bank performs OFAC and UN sanctions screening against the UBO list, matches the subscription agreement and board allotment resolution to the credit, and files the CBS inward-investment return on a T+1 basis; no same-day disbursement is permitted until the compliance officer clears the source-of-funds pack. Escrow release rule: funds remain in USD until the board records the due capital allocation; any conversion to WST for operational deployment requires the authorized-dealer FX conversion ticket and CBS exchange-control declaration.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for the CAD/BIM operating model: (i) sub-contractor design-fee payments to the PRC delivery entity — SWIFT MT103 corporate-to-corporate with strict invoice mapping, pre-registered beneficiary account, and purpose text 'SVC//BIM SUB-CONTRACT FEES PER OUTSOURCING AGREEMENT'; (ii) high-frequency contractor payroll — batch MT101 via BSP corporate e-banking using ISO 20022 pain.001 aggregated instructions; (iii) procurement of CAD software and compute infrastructure — irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit where vendors require documentary assurance, otherwise MT103 against vendor pro-forma invoices; (iv) intra-group cross-border sweeps from the USD Foreign Currency Account to the Hong Kong treasury — MT103 supported by a board-approved cash-pooling mandate and CBS outward capital-flow notification; (v) dividend or distribution remittance to shareholders — processed as a segregated MT103 only after the auditor's certificate, books-and-records declaration, and tax-clearance evidence are lodged, and never commingled with trade service payments.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore USD/WST outright FX forward (conventional, up to 12-month tenor) executed with an authorized dealer (BSP, NBS or SCB) under a bilateral ISDA 2002 or bank master FX line, permitted solely to hedge conversion of collected USD receivables into WST operating funds.
Onshore USD/WST FX swap (spot versus forward) through the authorized dealer for working-capital timing management.

Offshore USD/WST non-deliverable forward (NDF) — permissible only as a documented economic hedge backed by actual USD receivables, with prior CBS notification and an explicit prohibition of speculative or leveraged NDF positions.

Cross-currency swap between USD receivables and WST funding — available for larger infrastructure-grade contracts with Samoa-resident counterparties; requires CBS special approval and an auditable valuation methodology.
Vanilla FX options and structured derivatives — generally not available onshore; each transaction requires a CBS special licensing application as a non-bank hedging instrument.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Government Fee / Registration Renewal Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Apia, Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before the anniversary date of incorporation; SIFA issues an invoice at least 30 days before the due date and provides a 30-day grace period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty of 10% of the unpaid fee (minimum USD 100); non-payment continuing for 6 months after the due date triggers a Registrar's notice of intention to strike off; dissolution occurs 30 days after gazette publication, with assets vesting in the State

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return / Corporate Details Confirmation Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Apia, Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 30 days after each anniversary of incorporation, declaring directors, shareholders, registered agent, and registered office details
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Bundled within the annual fee; late filing incurs an administrative penalty of USD 100; persistent default for more than 6 months is a ground for administrative restriction orders and strike-off proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Apia, Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 days of the incorporation anniversary (filed concurrently with the annual return); any share transfer or UBO change must be lodged within 14 business days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Bundled within the annual fee; failure to file or knowingly filing false UBO data constitutes an offence under the International Companies (Beneficial Ownership) regime, exposing the company and each director to statutory fines up to USD 10,000 and strike-off in aggravated cases

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory audit applies to a tax-exempt Samoa International Company engaged solely in offshore civil-infrastructure BIM/CAD drafting. Mandatory independent audit is triggered only for (i) licensed banks, insurance, and trust companies; (ii) companies whose articles or shareholder resolution require an audit; or (iii) companies performing an economic-substance 'relevant activity' in Samoa with gross revenue above USD 1,000,000. The subject entity has no Samoa physical presence or local-source revenue and therefore falls below the trigger threshold.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted in Samoa for any audited or voluntarily published financial statements; equivalent recognized local GAAP acceptable for internal management accounts, provided the records give a true and fair view and fully support the tax-exempt status declaration.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The International Company must maintain a Register of Beneficial Owners at its registered office. Annually, within 30 days of the incorporation anniversary, the registered agent lodges a UBO confirmation statement confirming all material shareholdings, nominee relationships, and ultimate beneficial owners. Every share transfer or change in beneficial ownership requires director certification, updating of the statutory registers, and a notice to the Registrar within 14 business days; the annual confirmation must be re-signed by a director and countersigned by the registered agent.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 – USD 1,500 per annum for a licensed registered agent and registered office in Apia for a low-risk offshore IC with no local physical presence
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 – USD 9,000 per annum for a full IFRS-certified audit if voluntarily engaged or triggered; typically not required for a tax-exempt offshore drafting-services company

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% of net taxable income (Income Tax Act 1974, as amended; rate reduced from 27% effective tax year 2017)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Effective rate 0% for a qualifying International Company: International Companies Act 1987, s. 189 grants an absolute exemption from all Samoan income tax, capital gains, inheritance, stamp and other duties on the IC's assets, income and distributions for 20 years from the date of incorporation. No dividend or royalty WHT is levied on outbound payments by an IC. Non-resident-source income of any company is outside Samoa's territorial tax base.
